papers.title: Euclidean Methods on Dirac Quantization and Gauge Representation
papers.abstract: Geometrical interpretation on U(1) gage theory of Dirac monopole, introduced here from the line integral\cite{Brandt} form of vector potentials, shows the gauge representation be multi-valued. In this paper, we construct Euclidean form of U(1) gauge theory on Dirac monopole based on the geometrical interpretation, derive the Dirac quantization condition geometrically. Even several theoretical methods which leads to Dirac quantization $eg=l/2$ has been developed, these are only possible under the postulate that gauge representation is single-valued. Using the line integration representation of vector potential, we derived the gauge equation which satisfies under the `phase gauge transformation' ($\mathbf{A}\to\mathbf{A}'=\mathbf{A}, \ \psi\to\psi'=e^{ie\Lambda}\psi$), also showed that the Dirac quantization condition can be derived by the geometrical boundary condition on this gauge equation, without any supposing of canonical quantization condition. We finally explain geometrical meaning of constant phase of gauge and how the Dirac quantization holds single valued gauge representation.

papers.title: Understanding the normal state of cuprate superconductors
papers.abstract: Doped holes in the CuO2 planes reside pairwise at O atoms. Their lack of net charge demotes the flanking Cu3d-O2p holes of half-filling. Below the doping-dependent pseudogap (PG) temperature, the latter are trapped between motted Cu2+ ions. Above the PG temperature, the remaining Cu3d-O2p holes are thermally demotted, initiating the strange metal (SM) phase. The PG energy at the antinodal points in the BZ decreases with increasing doping, as less Cu3d-O2p holes need to be thermally demotted. In the SM phase, the Cu3d-O2p holes hop, with Planckian scattering rate, by leaps of lattice-constant length. This gives rise to a linear resistivity. O atoms in the CuO2 plane, from Sr doping of 214 cuprates or from oxygen enrichment (OE), arrange to a charge order (CO). In 214 systems, an O superlattice (SL) forms of increasing incommensurability with doping. It saturates when a secondary SL forms. At the quantum critical point their incommensurabilities equal, causing collapse of the PG temperature. In OE cuprates, the CO dilutes the diagonal tilt of the host lattice CuO6 octahedra, causing a decreasing incommensurability with doping. Oxygen atoms are singlets in OE cuprates but triplets in 214 systems. The magnetic moment of the latter gives rise to a narrow 3D AFM doping range and to magnetic order accompanying CO (stripes). Charge-density fluctuations occur when double holes hop back and forth between O atoms of the SL and neighboring oxygen ions. Quantum oscillations result from Fermi surface reconstruction.

papers.title: An empirically constrained low density regime Covariant Modified Gravity: accurate rendering of galactic rotation curves and lensing resulting in present accelerated cosmological expansion
papers.abstract: We present a covariant modified gravity theory calibrated to match all the galactic phenomenology usually attributed to dark matter in the low acceleration regime, including the flat rotation curves of massive tracers, and the deflection angles of photons as inferred through gravitational lensing. We first derive a fully covariant description of galactic space-times under a spherically symmetric and static approximation. This description accounts for flat rotation curves, observed gravitational lensing phenomenology and the Tully-Fisher mass scalings of the above. The resulting covariant description is then used to constrain the parameters of a minimally coupled gravitational action using power laws for both the Ricci scalar and the matter Lagrangian. The action presented hence leads to field equations whose trace, has as solutions metric coefficients which reproduce flat rotation curves and gravitational lensing observations, without including any dark matter. Using the same action for a FLRW metric results in a cosmology where a dust component behaves as effective dark energy with an equation of state $\omega=-5/6$, without the explicit inclusion of any dark energy component.
